title: St. Matthew Chapel
summary: St. Matthew Chapel is one of the surviving buildings associated with Freetown, an East Hampton neighborhood shaped by Black and Montaukett families. Built in 1852, the chapel served local worshippers before it was moved to the Maidstone Marina boatyard in 1976.
ancestral_territory_note: Shown in relation to Montaukett Ancestral Land on the current ancestral territory map.
why_this_matters: Originally located on Three Mile Harbor Road, St. Matthew's Chapel served as a shared community gathering space for Montaukett Indians, freed African Americans, and white residents of the Freetown neighborhood. Remembering this diverse congregation actively challenges the myth of Native disappearance, highlighting instead how Indigenous people forged complex social networks to survive and thrive within nineteenth-century working-class enclaves.
history_content:
1852. St. Matthew Chapel was built on the west side of Three Mile Harbor Road in Freetown. Accounts of the chapel connect it with Black and Montaukett residents, St. Luke's parishioners, and the congregation that later formed Calvary Baptist Church. The building had wooden floors, a bell, a stove, and stained glass behind the altar.

1976. The chapel was moved to the Maidstone Marina boatyard, now East Hampton Point, for use as a mariners' chapel. Local preservation work has since considered returning the building to a Freetown setting where its community history can be more fully interpreted.
